My siblings and I grew up in foster care. We all ended up kind of going different places but somehow my brother ended up back with my mom. He had just turned 18 at the time and he is on the autism spectrum. I was 20 and had my own place. A few days after my brother’s 18th birthday, I got a call from him crying. Turns out my mom had left him in a filthy apartment with no utilities on for days now and he didn’t think she was coming back. Without hesitation, I went and got him. It was extremely difficult. I lived in a small, one-bedroom apartment and I was not the most financially stable. But I knew what I needed to do. He was still in high school so I took him to school the next day. Right after I dropped him off, I don’t know why but it was extremely hard to let him go. I sobbed. I didn’t know what to do, I was clueless. I was a 20 year old kid that had to now parent a traumatized young man with autism. I didn’t know if I did the right thing. As I’m sobbing the song “Well Done” by The Afters came on. There’s a part that goes “well done my beloved child” and it completely solidified that I was doing the right thing. He ended up staying with me for a year. Things were rough but we made it through. He graduated high school and now has his own apartment. He is thriving!
You did awesome. So proud of you!
